stories.title: Iran says Lebanon conflict 'main topic' in US talks
stories.summary: Iran has said that the ongoing conflict in Lebanon between Israel and militant group Hezbollah will top the agenda in talks with the United States in Switzerland, as well as issues such as frozen Iranian funds and the sale of the country's oil. "The Zionist regime continues to violate its commitment in Lebanon, this issue will be the main topic of discussion in today's talks," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a video shared by IRNA state news agency. "The issue of making available Iran's frozen or restricted assets, as well as the discussion related to issuing the necessary licenses for the sale of Iranian oil," will also be on the agenda, he added. The first round of negotiations between the US and Iran since the two sides signed a preliminary agreement to halt their war is due to begin in Switzerland, with the conflict in Lebanon threatening the deal.

stories.title: Teenage boy dies following crash at Donegal Rally
stories.summary: A teenage boy has died and two others were injured following a crash during the Donegal International Rally. The accident happened during the 12th stage of the motorsport event, close to the village of Kilmacrennan. It is understood one of the competing cars veered close to the edge of a section of road, on the Gartan stage of the rally, and collided with a number of spectators. Three people were injured and transferred by ambulance to Letterkenny University Hospital.

stories.title: Drones and depravity - Sudan's 'abandoned' crisis
stories.summary: Peter Power, the head of the UN children's fund (UNICEF) in Ireland, has seen his fair share of conflicts and humanitarian crises around the world. He described the systematic sexual violence being used as a weapon of war as "beyond belief". That is being perpetrated mostly against women and girls and is particularly severe in the western Darfur region, which was the scene of the 2003-2005 genocide carried out by the notorious Janjaweed militia. In October last year, after an 18-month siege, the city of El Fasher, capital of the northern Darfur region, fell to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the successors to the Janjaweed.

stories.title: Man charged over series of attacks in Edinburgh - police
stories.summary: A 36-year-old man has been charged in connection with a series of attacks in Edinburgh, Police Scotland has said. British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the attacks appeared to be motivated by "anti-Muslim hatred". Counter-terrorism officers were brought in to investigate the attacks across Edinburgh on Friday which left five people injured. "A 36-year-old man has been charged in connection with a number of incidents which took place in Edinburgh on Friday, 19 June 2026," it said.

stories.title: AI meets Irish storytelling with robot seanchaí
stories.summary: An NCAD student has used AI to create a storytelling robot inspired by the seanchaí - traditional Irish storytellers - he grew up listening to. Nathan Costello, from Camp, Co Kerry, created his robot 'Cian' to be an oral archive of the Dingle Peninsula that people can hear stories from and tell stories to. "I think, over time, people would see the value in you being able to access an oral bank of stories, because so many stories are not written down. It’s important to have these traditional stories somewhere you can go." To build Cian’s catalogue, Nathan input stories he found on Dúchas.ie - the Irish National Folklore Collection, and brought the robot to towns and villages on the Dingle Peninsula to hear from people living there.

stories.title: Online shoppers facing new customs charges
stories.summary: If you regularly shop online for cheap items, new fees could make you reconsider your shopping habits. New EU customs charges could have significant implications for online shoppers who regularly buy low-cost items from British, Asian, American and other non-EU websites. From 1 July, a €3 Customs Duty charge per item will apply to all eCommerce packages valued at €150 or less coming into Ireland from outside the EU. The aim is to ensure fair competition for business and to protect consumers from risks posed from imports that don’t meet EU safety and compliance standards.
